context_requirements: Topical sunscreens act by absorbing or scattering UV photons in the stratum corneum; they have no defined intracellular protein target and require UV irradiation to exert their intended effect
These cell lines are cultured in the absence of UV light, so the pharmacological mechanism cannot be engaged
Any transcriptional response would require a secondary off-target activity (e.g. weak endocrine or oxidative effects) at 10 micromolar, which is not established for this class
falsifiers: A reproducible, dose-dependent signature of >20 landmark genes at 6 h in multiple lines with no UV exposure
Consistent induction of a specific nuclear-receptor or oxidative-stress program across all nine lines at 10 micromolar
Shared up-regulation of a coherent target set (e.g. CYP1A1/aryl-hydrocarbon or estrogen-responsive genes) that is absent in vehicle controls
